question: I just opened RackTrack for the first time. What am I looking at, and where do I start?
answer:
You are on the welcome screen. It is not a dashboard — it is the front door, and it has exactly one button that moves you forward.

On a phone (viewport under 768px, HomeLight):
1. You see the RackTrack logo and name at the top, a photo of a datacenter aisle, the headline "Manage your datacenter. From anywhere." and the line "Track racks, ports, and assets in real time."
2. If you are not signed in there is a Sign in button in the top-right corner, and the big button reads Get Started — it takes you to sign-up. Once you are signed in the Sign in button disappears.
3. If you are already signed in, Get Started takes you straight to the Scan screen. That is the intended first move: tap Get Started, then scan a rack.

On an iPad or a computer (768px and wider, HomeStudio) the same screen is laid out side by side: a small kicker line ("AI rack intelligence", or "Welcome back, <your name>" once you are signed in), the headline "See every port. Know every rack.", a paragraph explaining what RackTrack does, three figures (30+ device classes, 0.3s per rack, 98% accuracy), and a datacenter photo on the right marked LIVE SCAN with a sample status strip (CHENNAI-DC1 - 24 racks - 1,048 ports mapped; that strip is illustrative, not your data). The main button reads Get started when signed out and Start a scan once you are signed in. When you are signed in a second button, Past scans, appears next to it — it opens your Profile page, where your scan history lives. The top-right button is Sign in when signed out and Sign out when signed in.

There is nothing actionable beyond that on this screen. The rest of the app opens up once you tap through to Scan.
symptoms: First time opening the app
The home screen has nothing on it
Where do I start
Only a Get Started button
What is this welcome page
rootCause: The '/' route renders HomePage, which immediately delegates to HomeStudio (>=768px viewport) or HomeLight (phones). Both are marketing-style welcome screens whose only forward action is a CTA that routes to /scan when authenticated or /signup when not.

question: A four-step introduction popped up the first time I signed in. Can I get it back?
answer:
No — the walkthrough is shown once per device and there is no button anywhere in the app to replay it. Signing out and back in will not bring it back either.

What it said, so you do not need it again:
1. "Welcome to RackTrack" — turn a photo of a server rack into a full, labelled map of what's inside, in seconds.
2. "1 · Scan a rack" — point your camera at the rack (or upload a photo or short video) and tap Scan.
3. "2 · Review the results" — see each device, where it sits in the rack, and its details. Tap any item to dig deeper or fix a label.
4. "3 · Check the ports" — open the Ports tab to see the switch live: which ports are free, which are connected, and what's plugged in.

The controls are Skip in the top-right corner, Next to move forward (Back appears from the second card onwards), and on the last card Start scanning, which drops you on the Scan screen. Skipping counts as finishing — it will not come back either way.

It only appears when you are signed in, so if you sign in on a second phone or tablet you will see it again there. Reinstalling the app, or otherwise clearing the app's local storage on a device, would also make it reappear, but there is no supported in-app way to reset it.
symptoms: Intro tour disappeared
How do I see the tutorial again
Welcome to RackTrack popup
I skipped the walkthrough by accident
Getting started guide
rootCause: OnboardingTour records completion in localStorage under the key 'racktrack:onboarded' and returns null forever after; it also renders only when isAuthed. No UI resets the flag.

question: I tapped HOME at the bottom and the menu bar vanished. Now I can't get anywhere.
answer:
That is how the home screen is built — it deliberately has no bottom bar and no sidebar. It is the welcome screen, not a hub.

To get moving again:
1. On a phone, tap Get Started — the big button in the middle. Since you are signed in it takes you straight to the Scan screen, where the bottom bar with HOME, SCAN and PROFILE comes back.
2. On an iPad or computer (768px wide and up) the welcome screen shows Start a scan and, next to it, Past scans. Start a scan goes to Scan; Past scans goes to Profile. Both bring the left sidebar back.
3. Do not rely on the back gesture on the Android app: on the home screen the hardware/gesture back is wired to exit RackTrack, not to go back a page. (In a browser, back does return you to the previous screen.)

Practical advice: on a phone, treat SCAN and PROFILE as your two real destinations — HOME only returns you to the welcome screen. On an iPad or computer the sidebar is present on the normal app screens (Scan, Profile, Results, Ports, Topology and so on), and clicking Home in that sidebar drops it again until you navigate on. A few full-page screens — sign in, sign up, the pending-approval wait screen and the Organizations console — also have no sidebar by design.
symptoms: Bottom bar disappeared
Nav bar missing on home screen
Tapped HOME and got stuck
No menu on the welcome page
Sidebar gone after clicking Home
rootCause: In App.jsx the '/' route renders <HomePage /> bare — it is not wrapped in ResponsiveLayout, so neither BottomNav (phone) nor DesktopShell (>=768px) is mounted. Only routes passed withBottomNav render the bottom bar.

{/* HomePage has its own desktop branch (HomeDesktop) via
    useIsDesktop, so DesktopShell is bypassed for "/" —
    otherwise we'd double-render the chrome. */}
<Route path="/" element={<HomePage />} />

<Route path="/scan" element={
  <ProtectedRoute><ResponsiveLayout withBottomNav><ScanPage /></ResponsiveLayout></ProtectedRoute>
} />

question: The app looks totally different on my phone, my iPad and my laptop. Which one is right?
answer:
All three are right — RackTrack has three layouts and switches between them purely on how wide the screen is. Nothing is broken and there is no setting to change it.

- Narrower than 768 pixels (any phone, and an iPad app window that has been split small): the phone layout, with no sidebar. Most pages pin a bar to the bottom with HOME, SCAN and PROFILE. A few do not: the rack result pages show their own tab strip along the bottom instead (Overview / Ports / Topology / Network / Switches / Drift), and Two racks, Console and Data Sources show no bottom bar at all.
- 768 pixels and wider (iPad in portrait or landscape, small laptop windows): the sidebar appears down the left with Home, Scan, Two racks and Profile — plus Console and Lab for the platform owner, and Data Sources and Marketplace for organization admins. The bottom bar disappears completely, and once you have scanned a rack the sidebar also lists that rack's Overview / Ports / Topology / Network / Switches / Drift.
- 1024 pixels and wider (laptops, desktop browsers, iPad landscape): the same sidebar, but pages that have a wide layout switch to it — most visibly, the rack tab strip is dropped from the page because the sidebar already carries the same links.

So an iPad in portrait sits between the two: it gets the sidebar but still uses the phone-width page layouts, which is why on a portrait iPad you can briefly see the rack tabs in both the sidebar and the page. If you rotate the iPad or resize the browser window, the layout changes live — you do not need to reload.

One exception at every size: the welcome screen at Home has neither the bottom bar nor the sidebar. It does change appearance at 768 pixels — a simpler welcome on phones, a richer one on tablets and laptops — but that is a different page design, not different navigation.
symptoms: Different layout on iPad vs phone
Sidebar on laptop but not on phone
Layout changed when I rotated the tablet
Which layout is correct
App looks different on desktop
rootCause: Two breakpoints drive everything: SIDEBAR_BREAKPOINT = 768 (useHasSidebar -> DesktopShell vs bare mobile + BottomNav) and DESKTOP_BREAKPOINT = 1024 (useIsDesktop -> wide content layouts, e.g. suppressing ScanTabBar). Both are matchMedia hooks so they re-evaluate on resize/rotation.

question: The welcome screen on my iPad has different buttons from the one on my phone. Why?
answer:
There are two different welcome screens and the app picks one purely by browser/screen width — 768 pixels is the cut-off (HomePage renders HomeStudio at 768px and above, HomeLight below). Rotating an iPad or resizing a browser window switches you between them live.

Phone welcome screen (under 768px): logo and the RackTrack name, a Sign in button top-right that appears only when you are signed out, a datacenter photo, the headline "Manage your datacenter. From anywhere." with the line "Track racks, ports, and assets in real time.", and one button, Get Started.

iPad / computer welcome screen (768px and up): a two-column layout. On the left a small line reading "AI rack intelligence" — which becomes "Welcome back, <your username>" once you are signed in — the headline "See every port. Know every rack.", a short description, then the buttons. The buttons depend on whether you are signed in: signed out you get a single Get started button; signed in that same button becomes Start a scan and a second Past scans button appears next to it. So Get Started has not disappeared on iPad — it is there until you sign in, at which point it is renamed Start a scan. Below that are three figures: 30+ device classes, 0.3s per rack, 98% accuracy. On the right is a photo tagged LIVE SCAN with a scanning overlay and a strip reading CHENNAI-DC1 · 24 racks · 1,048 ports mapped.

Those three figures and the CHENNAI-DC1 strip are fixed illustration text written into the welcome screen itself. They are not your organization's numbers, they are not fetched from the server, and they never change — so nothing is wrong if 24 racks or 1,048 ports does not match your site.

The top-right button also differs between the two screens: on the phone screen it offers Sign in and is hidden entirely once you are signed in. On the iPad/computer screen it is always visible and switches to Sign out once you are signed in.
symptoms: Different home screen on tablet
Where did Get Started go on my iPad
24 racks 1,048 ports is wrong
Home page shows numbers I don't recognise
Welcome back message only on desktop
rootCause: HomePage branches on useIsTabletOrUp (TABLET_BREAKPOINT = 768): HomeStudio above, HomeLight below. HomeStudio's stats and HUD strip are hard-coded literals in the component, not fetched data.

question: I clicked the button in the top-right of the home screen on my laptop and it signed me straight out with no warning.
answer:
That button is Sign out, and on the home screen it takes effect immediately — there is no "are you sure?" step there.

What happened: on an iPad or computer, the home screen's top-right button shows Sign in with an arrow icon when you are signed out, and swaps to Sign out once you are signed in. Pressing it signs you out and returns you to the home screen straight away.

To get back in, press Sign in in that same corner and enter your credentials. Nothing is lost — your scans stay on the server and your Recent Scans list is intact when you sign back in.

If you want the safer version, sign out from Profile instead: the exit icon in the Profile header asks "Sign out?" with the note "You'll need to sign in again to scan racks." and gives you a Cancel button. The phone home screen never shows a Sign out button at all — it only offers Sign in, and only when you are signed out.
symptoms: Signed out by accident
No confirmation before sign out
Clicked top right and lost my session
Sign out button on the home page
rootCause: HomeStudio's header button calls auth.logout() then navigate('/') directly with no confirmation dialog, unlike ProfilePage which gates sign-out behind a confirm modal.

  className={styles.signBtn}
  onClick={authed ? () => { auth.logout(); navigate('/'); } : () => navigate('/login')}

question: I pressed the back arrow on my scan result and it threw me out to the Scan screen. How do I get the result back?
answer:
The back arrow on a rack result means "go back one tab", and on the Overview tab it means "leave this rack" — which lands you on the Scan screen. That is deliberate, not a bug.

Exactly what the arrow does:
- On the Overview tab: leaves the rack entirely and goes to Scan.
- On any other tab (Switches, Ports, Topology, Network, Drift): steps back through the tabs you opened, in the order you opened them. When there are none left, it returns you to Overview. Press it again from Overview and you leave the rack.

To get the result back:
1. Open PROFILE and find the rack under Recent Scans — tap it to reopen. (On an iPad or computer the sidebar also keeps a "Rack · <rack ID>" section pointing at the rack you were on.)
2. Or, if you still have the rack's web address, open it again — a /results/<rack ID> link reopens the rack from the server.

Tip: the rack ID is printed under the title at the top of the result screen, so note it down if you are moving between racks a lot.
symptoms: Back button leaves the scan result
Lost my results after pressing back
Back arrow goes to the upload screen
How do I return to my scan
rootCause: ResultsPage.handleHeaderBack navigates to /scan whenever tab === 'overview'; on other tabs it pops tabHistoryRef (the in-page tab stack) and otherwise falls back to the overview tab.

{rackId || scanId}

question: The phone's back gesture doesn't step back through the rack tabs — it jumps out of the result completely.
answer:
Use the back arrow inside the app (top-left of the result screen) or the bottom tab strip, not the phone's back gesture, to move between a rack's tabs.

Why: switching between Overview, Switches, Ports, Topology, Network and Drift on a phone does not change the web address — the whole rack lives at one address and the tabs swap the content in place. Your phone's back gesture only knows about address changes, so it skips the tabs entirely and takes you to the screen you were on before you opened the rack.

What to use instead:
- The back arrow in the result's own header steps back through the tabs you visited, in order — but only while you are on a tab other than Overview. Overview is treated as the root of the rack: pressing back there always leaves the rack and returns you to the scan screen, and it also clears the remembered tab history. If you are on another tab and there is no history to step back through, back returns you to Overview.
- The tab strip fixed at the bottom of the result (Overview, Switches, Ports, Topology, and More for Network and Drift) jumps anywhere directly, and is the most reliable way to move around. Note this strip is mobile-only; on desktop the same links live in the left sidebar.

On Android specifically, the hardware back button walks the app's page history (the previous screen, not the previous tab) and, on the home screen or the sign-in screen, closes RackTrack.
symptoms: Back gesture exits the rack
Android back button skips the tabs
Swipe back goes too far
Browser back loses my place in the result
rootCause: The rack tab strip changes React state via handleTabChange (setTab + tabHistoryRef) without touching the URL, so browser/OS history has no entry per tab. AndroidBackHandler maps the hardware back button to navigate(-1), i.e. the previous route, or exitApp on '/' and '/login'.

question: On my iPad the rack tabs appear twice — once in the left sidebar and once as a strip in the page. Is that a display fault?
answer:
It is not a fault, and both sets do the same thing — it is a side-effect of the iPad's width.

RackTrack shows the left sidebar from 768 pixels wide, but only hides the rack tab bar from 1024 pixels wide. An iPad in portrait is roughly 768–834 pixels, so it lands between the two and gets both.

What to do: use either. The sidebar section is headed "Rack · <rack ID>" and holds Overview, Ports, Topology, Network, Switches and Drift. The other set is a tab bar pinned along the bottom of the screen (not a strip in the page body); it holds Overview, Switches, Ports, Topology and a More button that opens Network and Drift. There is one small difference worth knowing — the bottom bar also shows small count badges: on Ports, the combined port count of all switches found in the rack, and on Switches, how many switches were found.

If you would rather see only one set, turn the iPad to landscape: past 1024 pixels the bottom tab bar is hidden and the sidebar becomes the only rack navigation.
symptoms: Two sets of tabs on iPad
Duplicate navigation on tablet
Rack tabs shown twice
Tab strip and sidebar both visible
rootCause: DesktopShell mounts at useHasSidebar() >= 768px, while ResultsPage suppresses ScanTabBar only when useIsDesktop() >= 1024px. Viewports in the 768-1023px band therefore render both navigations.

question: I typed an address (or followed an old link) and RackTrack dumped me on the welcome screen.
answer:
The welcome screen is where RackTrack sends anything it cannot open. Three different things land you there:

1. The address does not exist. Any unrecognised address — a typo, a link to a page that was removed — is redirected to the home screen rather than showing a "page not found" error. Check the spelling and try again. Two old addresses are deliberate exceptions and still work: an old /logs bookmark opens the Operations Console, and an old /history bookmark opens Profile.
2. The page is restricted and you do not have the role for it. Data Sources, Marketplace and the Operations Console are limited to organization admins and the platform owner; if you are a member or a site manager, opening those addresses directly bounces you to home instead of showing an error. Ask your organization admin.
3. You are in the Organizations console and pressed App — that button is a deliberate exit back to the main app.

Different symptom, different cause: if you land on the Scan screen rather than the welcome screen, the address was a valid rack link but that scan no longer exists on the server. If you land on the Sign in screen, your session ended. And if you land on the "waiting for approval" screen, your organization has not been approved yet.
symptoms: Redirected to the home page
Link goes nowhere
No 404 page
Typed a URL and got the welcome screen
Bounced back to home when opening a page
rootCause: App.jsx has a catch-all <Route path="*" element={<Navigate to="/" replace />} /> so unknown paths redirect home, and AdminRoute redirects non-(org_admin|owner) users to '/'. There is no 404 page in the route table.

evidence.snippet: <Route path="*" element={<Navigate to="/" replace />} />

question: I scanned two racks together — how do I get from one rack to the other, and why did the switcher disappear?
answer:
A multi-rack scan puts a small sticky strip across the top of the result. It holds one pill per rack, numbered — #1, #2 — with each rack's label, plus a small "3D" button on the right that opens all the racks in one combined scene.

How to use it:
1. Tap the other rack's pill. You stay on the same sub-page — if you were on Ports for rack 1, you land on Ports for rack 2. (The strip appears on the Overview, Ports and Topology pages; it is not shown on Netdisco.)
2. The rack you are currently viewing is the pill that is filled in solid/highlighted — it cannot be tapped. The other racks are the outlined, grey pills you can tap. That is how you tell which rack you are on.
3. Tap 3D to open all the racks in one scene with the cabling that runs between them.

If the strip has disappeared, the link you followed lost the group marker that tells RackTrack these racks belong together. RackTrack only shows the strip when the address carries a ?group=<group ID> marker that matches the rack's real group and the group has at least two racks. Opening a plain /results/<rack ID> address — which is what your Recent Scans list links to — or hand-editing the address drops that marker. The rack itself opens fine, just on its own. To get the group back, follow the link you were given for the multi-rack scan, or re-open the combined view. A single-rack scan never shows the strip at all — and re-uploading a photo that was once part of a multi-rack scan still gives you a single-rack report, by design.
symptoms: Can't switch between the two racks
Rack pills missing
Two-rack scan only shows one rack
Where is the 3D button
Rack strip disappeared
rootCause: RackTabs renders only when useGroupView reports isGroup, which depends on the ?group query parameter being present on the URL. Navigating to a bare /results/<rackId> (e.g. from Recent Scans) drops that signal, so the group strip is not rendered.

question: The title bar on my laptop says "Live Network Switch" but I clicked Ports. Am I on the wrong page?
answer:
You are on the right page. On a laptop, desktop browser or iPad, the strip above the page content is a location label, and a few of them are worded differently from the menu item you clicked.

The ones that catch people out:
- Ports (rack) shows as "Live Network Switch — Available ports".
- Network (rack) shows as "Network view — Live device + port table".
- Topology (rack) shows as "Topology — 3D rack & cabling".
- Switches (rack) shows as "Switch info — CMDB-driven".
- Scan shows as "New scan — Upload, camera, or video".
- Two racks shows as "Scan two racks — Detect both + the cabling between them".

A few screens do not show that strip at all — the Operations Console (Console), Profile, Data Sources and every Marketplace page draw their own heading instead, so there is no second title stacked on top. That is why clicking Console gives you no strip: the page's own "Operations Console" header is the only title there.

If the strip ever just says "RackTrack" with nothing under it, you are on a page that has no label of its own; the left sidebar still shows which item is highlighted.

On the rack's Ports page there is also a small back arrow to the left of the title — that walks you back one step.
symptoms: Page title doesn't match the menu item
Live Network Switch heading
Breadcrumb says something else
Title bar says RackTrack
No title bar on the Profile page
rootCause: DesktopShell derives the topbar crumb from a PAGE_TITLE map plus deriveTitle() suffix rules; SELF_HEADED paths (/dashboard, /profile, /connections) and every /marketplace* path suppress the crumb because those pages render their own header.

question: INTERNAL: which home component actually renders, and is HomeDesktop still in use?
answer:
HomeDesktop.jsx is dead code. Nothing imports it — the only remaining references are its own file/CSS module, a passing mention in index.css (line ~205), and a stale comment in App.jsx above the '/' route claiming "HomePage has its own desktop branch (HomeDesktop) via useIsDesktop". That is no longer true.

What actually runs for '/':
- App.jsx (line 229) renders <HomePage /> bare (no ResponsiveLayout), so '/' has no DesktopShell and no BottomNav at any width.
- HomePage.jsx contains no markup of its own any more: the component ends with `const isTabletOrUp = useIsTabletOrUp(); if (isTabletOrUp) return <HomeStudio />; return <HomeLight />;`. Its local state, RACKS, SCREENS, the Rack3D helper and the drag-to-rotate handlers still execute as plain code on each render but nothing they feed is ever rendered.
- Breakpoint is useIsTabletOrUp (768px, iPad portrait), not useIsDesktop (1024px) — so desktop widths also land on HomeStudio, which is why HomeDesktop can never appear.
- HomeStudio portals to document.body to escape #root's 540px max-width column cap; DesktopShell does the same.

Support implications: never tell a customer about HomeDesktop's copy ("Scan the rack. Know everything.", the four "How it works" step cards, the RACK-U42-DEMO hero visual) — that page cannot be reached from the running app. The tablet/desktop welcome copy is HomeStudio's ("See every port. / Know every rack."). Do not quote HomePage's demo racks either: R-101 and R-102 (Chennai-DC1), R-103 (Hyderabad-DC2), incidents INC0042/INC0058, or its 3D rack views — all dead data inside HomePage.jsx.
symptoms: Which home screen does the user see
HomeDesktop copy doesn't match the app
Screenshot doesn't match the code
R-101 rack not in my account
rootCause: HomePage.jsx short-circuits to HomeStudio/HomeLight before rendering any of its own markup, and HomeDesktop.jsx has no importers; the App.jsx comment referencing it was not updated.

<Route path="/" element={<HomePage />} />

question: INTERNAL: full navigation reference — which route renders which chrome, and who can reach it?
answer:
Same as the entry, with two precisions:

1. DesktopShell = sidebar + crumb topbar, portalled to document.body — but the crumb topbar is suppressed on pages that draw their own header: SELF_HEADED = ['/dashboard', '/profile', '/connections'] plus '/marketplace' and every '/marketplace/*' path (those render MarketplaceShell). On those routes at >=768px you get the sidebar and full-width canvas but no breadcrumb bar. (Note the "≥1024px" comments in App.jsx/DesktopShell are stale — the shell gate is useHasSidebar() at SIDEBAR_BREAKPOINT = 768; useIsDesktop()'s 1024 breakpoint is only used by content layouts such as side-by-side racks.)

2. The remembered rack id (module-level _liveRackId, never stored in session/localStorage) is set from the URL (/results/<id> or /switch-info/<id>) or from a rt:rack-id-changed event. That event is dispatched with a rack id by ResultsPage after an upload finishes, and with null/'' by AuthContext on login and logout and by ScanPage when a new scan starts — so it is cleared on refresh, on login/logout, on starting a new scan, and on landing on /scan.

Everything else in the entry (route/chrome table, withBottomNav list, ProtectedRoute/AdminRoute/PendingRoute behaviour, server-side requireRole('owner') on /api/lab/*, the /logs -> /dashboard, /history -> /profile and * -> / redirects, and the sidebar link visibility rules) matches the source exactly.

Why does this page have no menu
Who can reach which route
rootCause: Navigation chrome is decided per-route by whether the element is wrapped in ResponsiveLayout and whether withBottomNav is passed; role gating is done by the ProtectedRoute / AdminRoute / PendingRoute wrappers plus DesktopShell's conditional link array.
